Create test items

Create two bought items and one made item, with the defaults, bill of material and routing a production order needs.

Status
Walked 3 of 10
Module
Common, Procurement, Manufacturing, Warehousing
Code
D2R-02, D2R-07, D2R-05, D2R-09
Length
10 tasks, 124 steps
Updated
12 Nov 2026

Start

Summary

TaskWhat you doResultSteps
1Choose the site, warehouses and unitsYou've written down the site, a warehouse for bought materials, a warehouse for finished items, and the units7
2Create two item groupsThere are two new item groups, one for bought items and one for made items7

Before you start

  • You need a training company you're allowed to add item groups and defaults to.
  • You need a work center and a reference operation at your site. This guide doesn't make them. Find them in Work Centers (tirou0101m000) and Reference Operations (tirou4150m000). If there are none, ask whoever set up the plant.

Procedure

1Choose the site, warehouses and units

Result
You've written down the site, a warehouse for bought materials, a warehouse for finished items, and the units.
Session
Warehousing➔Master Data➔Warehouses➔Warehouses (whwmd2500m000)

Why LN works this way. Nothing changes yet. The later tasks use what you write down here. Check each warehouse's type: you can't receive goods into a Shop Floor warehouse, and the name doesn't tell you the type.

StepActionYou should see
1.1Filter the list to the site that will buy, make and sell the test itemsThe warehouses at that siteWrite downsite
1.2Find a warehouse for bought materials whose Warehouse Type is NormalWrite downraw-material warehouse
1.3Find a warehouse for finished items whose Warehouse Type is NormalWrite downfinished-goods warehouse
1.4Open Master Data➔Items➔ItemsItems (tcibd0501m000) opens
1.5Open an existing physical item that's counted the same way as your test items will beItem (tcibd0501m100) opens
1.6Read Unit Set and UnitWrite downunit setunit
1.7Search the list for each item code you plan to useNo item has any of your codes
Choose the site, warehouses and units: if something goes wrong
SymptomWhat to do
An item code you planned is already usedChoose another code. Don't change or reuse an existing item
The warehouse for materials is a Shop Floor warehouseYou can't receive into it. Choose one whose Warehouse Type is Normal

2Create two item groups

Result
There are two new item groups, one for bought items and one for made items.
Session
Master Data➔Items➔Item Classification➔Item Groups (tcmcs0123m000)

Why LN works this way. LN keeps item defaults for each item type and item group. Bought and made items need different defaults, so each gets a group of its own. A new group is only a code, a description and a currency until the next tasks give it defaults.

StepActionYou should see
2.1Search for the group code you plan to use for bought itemsNo group has that code
2.2Click NewA new row
2.3Enter the code in Item GroupExampleItem Group BAM-RM for bought items, BAM-FG for made itemsWrite downgroup for bought items
2.4Enter a DescriptionExampleDescription Bamboo Raw Materials, Bamboo Finished Goods
2.5Set Currency to your company's currency
2.6Click SaveThe group is listed
2.7Do steps 2.1 to 2.6 again for made itemsWrite downgroup for made items
Create two item groups: if something goes wrong
SymptomWhat to do
A group code is already usedChoose another code. Don't change a group someone else uses

3Set the defaults for bought items

Result
Your group for bought items has Ordering, Purchase and Warehousing defaults, each with Create ticked.
Session
Master Data➔Items➔Defaults➔Item Defaults (tcibd0102m000)

Why LN works this way. Each kind of item data has two settings here. The indicator shows that default data exists, and the Create box decides whether a new item gets it. An indicator that's on with Create clear gives a new item nothing. The Sites box decides whether a new item gets a site row by itself.

StepActionYou should see
3.1Filter on your group for bought items from step 2.3No row yet
3.2Click NewItem Defaults (tcibd0502m000) opens, empty, with Item Type Product
3.3Click into Item Group and enter your group for bought itemsIts description appears beside it
3.4Choose Unit Set from its lookup: the unit set from step 1.6
3.5Choose Inventory Unit from its lookup: the unit from step 1.6
3.6Leave the other fields as LN fills them in
3.7Click SaveThe status bar says Modify
3.8Open the Sites tabNo rows
3.9On the Sites grid, click New, enter the site from step 1.1 and press TabThe site's name and city appear
3.10Enter the raw-material warehouse from step 1.2 in WarehouseIts name appears
3.11Check Supply SourcePurchase
3.12Click SaveThe site row stays
3.13Click the blue Ordering linkItem Ordering Defaults (tcibd2101m000) opens
3.14Leave the fields as LN fills them in, and click OKThe screen closes with no error, and the indicator beside Ordering is on
3.15Tick Create beside Ordering
3.16Click the blue Purchase linkItems - Purchase Defaults (tdipu0102m000) opens
3.17Fill in Purchase Unit, Purchase Price Unit, Purchase Currency and Purchase Price Group, and on the second tab Purchase Statistics Group, as an existing group for bought items has them
3.18Click OK and tick Create beside PurchaseThe indicator beside Purchase is on
3.19Do steps 3.13 to 3.15 for WarehousingItems - Warehousing Defaults (whwmd4101s000) opens, with Location Controlled ticked
3.20Under Create Satellites Automatically, tick Sites
3.21Click Save, then RefreshThree indicators on, three Create boxes ticked, and Sites ticked
Set the defaults for bought items: if something goes wrong
SymptomWhat to do
Product isn't in the Item Type listProduct items may be switched off in your company. Ask whoever set it up. Don't use Purchased or Manufactured instead
Ordering defaults seem to need a warehouse, but there's no Warehouse fieldThe warehouse comes from the site row. Check it at step 3.10
Ordering defaults won't saveFill in every field the screen says is needed, and leave Economic Order Quantity as LN filled it in
Purchase defaults won't saveCheck the units, the currency, the price group and the statistics group
Warehousing defaults ask for a value you don't knowStop and ask whoever owns the warehouse setup. Don't make up a value

4Set the defaults for made items

Result
Your group for made items has Ordering, Production, Warehousing and Sales defaults, each with Create ticked.
Session
Master Data➔Items➔Defaults➔Item Defaults (tcibd0102m000)

Why LN works this way. It works like the defaults for bought items, with a different supply source and two more kinds of data, Production and Sales. Job Shop means you make the item in your own plant. Changing Sales defaults offers to update existing items too. Your group is new, so you answer No.

StepActionYou should see
4.1Filter on your group for made items from step 2.7No row yet
4.2Click NewItem Defaults (tcibd0502m000) opens, empty, with Item Type Product
4.3Click into Item Group and enter your group for made itemsIts description appears beside it
4.4Do steps 3.4 to 3.9The site row
4.5Enter the finished-goods warehouse from step 1.3 in WarehouseIts name appears
4.6Set Supply Source to Job Shop
4.7Click SaveThe site row stays
4.8Do steps 3.13 to 3.15 for Ordering, then for WarehousingBoth indicators on, and both Create boxes ticked
4.9Click the blue Production linkItem Production Defaults (tiipd0102m100) opens
4.10Leave the fields as LN fills them in, and click OKThe screen closes with no error, and the indicator beside Production is on
4.11Tick Create beside Production
4.12Click the blue Sales linkItem Sales Defaults (tdisa0102s000) opens
4.13On the Ordering tab, fill in Sales Unit
4.14On the Price tab, check Sales Currency is your company's currency, and fill in Sales Price Unit, Sales Price Group, Sales Statistics Group and Tax Code as an existing group for finished items has them
4.15Click OKThe indicator beside Sales is on
4.16If LN asks Perform Global Update of Sales Items with New Defaults?, click No. If Global Update of Item with Defaults (tdisa0202m000) opens, click Close, not UpdateExisting items stay as they are
4.17Tick Create beside Sales
4.18Under Create Satellites Automatically, tick Sites
4.19Click Save, then RefreshFour indicators on, four Create boxes ticked, and Sites ticked
Set the defaults for made items: if something goes wrong
SymptomWhat to do
The Production link doesn't openJob Shop by Site may be switched off in your company. Ask whoever set it up
The finished-goods group you copy from shows another currencyUse your company's currency. Sales takes its currency from the company

5Check the site follows the defaults

Result
At your site, each group creates the same kinds of item data as its defaults.
Session
Master Data➔Items➔Defaults➔Item Control and Defaults by Site (tcibd1552m000)

Why LN works this way. A site can decide for itself which item data a new item gets. When Centrally Managed is ticked, the site copies the company defaults and the boxes here are greyed. When it's clear, the boxes here decide. If they don't match the defaults, a new item comes out missing data and LN doesn't say why.

StepActionYou should see
5.1Open the row for your site, Product and your group for bought itemsThe row opens
5.2Look at Centrally ManagedIt's ticked or clear
5.3If it's ticked, check Ordering, Purchase and WarehousingAll three are ticked and greyed
5.4If it's clear, tick Ordering, Purchase and Warehousing
5.5If you ticked them, click Save
5.6Do steps 5.1 to 5.5 for your group for made items, with Ordering, Production, Warehousing and SalesAll four are ticked
Check the site follows the defaults: if something goes wrong
SymptomWhat to do
A box is greyed and you need to change itCentrally Managed is ticked, so the site copies the defaults. Change Create in the defaults instead, at step 3.19

6Create the three items

Result
The three items are saved, and each site row shows the supply source and item data its group gives.
Session
Master Data➔Items➔Items (tcibd0501m000)

Why LN works this way. When you save, LN gives the item its group's supply source, units and item data. If Sites was ticked in the defaults, it adds a site row too. The site row is where you check the defaults worked. That's why you don't type what LN fills in: a value you type would hide a mistake in the defaults.

StepActionYou should see
6.1Click NewItem (tcibd0501m100) opens, empty. It can take half a minute
6.2Item has two boxes. Leave the first, for a project, empty. Type the first bought item's code in the secondExampleItem BAM-ROD, then BAM-SLEEVE, then BAM-CHOP-PAIRWrite downitem code
6.3Click into Description and enter oneExampleDescription Bamboo Rod, then Paper Sleeve, then Bamboo Chopstick Pair
6.4Check Item TypeProduct
6.5Click into Item Group and enter the item's group from Create two item groupsUnit Set and Unit fill in
6.6Fill in any other field the screen says is needed
6.7Click SaveThe item is saved, and the Subentities indicators of its group turn green
6.8Look at the Sites gridA row for your site, with Default Supply Source filled in. The top row, marked =, is a filter, not a site
6.9If there's no row for your site, choose Create Items by Site from the Sites tab's menuA row for your site
6.10Open your site's row with the arrow at its startItems by Site (tcibd1550m000) opens for this item and site
6.11Check Default Supply SourcePurchase for a bought item, Job Shop for a made one
6.12Check which kinds of item data are onOrdering, Purchase and Warehousing for a bought item. Ordering, Production, Warehousing and Sales for a made one
6.13Do steps 6.1 to 6.12 for the second bought item, then for the made itemEach item's site row matches its group
Create the three items: if something goes wrong
SymptomWhat to do
LN won't take the item codeChoose a code that follows your company's pattern for item codes. Don't change the pattern for a test
The code goes into the project box, or General Projects opensClose it without making a project. Clear both boxes and type the code in the second
The save is refused for a field this guide doesn't nameWrite down the field and the message, then fill it in. Don't clear another field to make it save
Create Items by Site makes no rowClick New on the Sites toolbar, choose your site, and save
A kind of item data is missing after you saveCheck the defaults: Set the defaults for bought items for a bought item, Set the defaults for made items for the made one, and Check the site follows the defaults for both
The supply source isn't the one the group givesThe item or the site may have its own value, or one that starts on a later date. Check those before you change the defaults

7Build the bill of material

Result
The made item has an Approved BOM with both materials, used for planning and for costing.
Session
Manufacturing➔Job Shop➔Engineering➔Bills of Material (tibom3100m000)

Why LN works this way. A BOM lists what one item is made from, at one site. LN only makes items from an approved BOM. Approving it, using it for planning and using it for costing are three separate actions. Each material line says which warehouse the material comes from.

StepActionYou should see
7.1Check Site at the top is the site from step 1.1Only that site's BOMs are listed
7.2Filter Product on the made itemNo BOM for it yet
7.3Click NewJob Shop Bill of Material (tibom3600m000) opens, empty
7.4Set Product to the made item
7.5Set BOM Quantity to 1
7.6Set Effective Date to the day of your production order, or earlierExampleEffective Date today
7.7Leave Routing empty
7.8Click SaveStatus = NewWrite downBOM and revision
7.9In a new line of the materials grid below the header, enter the first bought item in ItemExampleItem BAM-ROD, then BAM-SLEEVE
7.10Enter how many go into one made item in Net QuantityExampleNet Quantity 2 for BAM-ROD, 1 for BAM-SLEEVE
7.11Check the line's WarehouseThe raw-material warehouse from step 1.2
7.12Do steps 7.9 to 7.11 for the second bought itemTwo lines
7.13Leave Scrap Percentage and Scrap Quantity at 0
7.14Click SaveBoth lines are saved
7.15Go back to Job Shop Bills of Material and tick your BOM's row
7.16Actions➔Revision➔Approve RevisionLN says the revision was approved
7.17Actions➔Use➔Use for Planning
7.18Actions➔Use➔Use for CostingUse for Planning and Use for Costing have green ticks
Build the bill of material: if something goes wrong
SymptomWhat to do
The BOM won't saveCheck Site, Product, BOM Quantity and Effective Date. Don't clear a value LN filled in to make it save
The BOM stays NewLN only makes items from an approved BOM. Tick its row and choose Actions➔Revision➔Approve Revision
LN refuses Use for PlanningAnother BOM already has it. Only one BOM per item and site can be used for planning, and one per item for costing
The production order has no materialsIts date is before the BOM's Effective Date. See step 7.6

8Build the routing

Result
The made item has an Approved routing with one operation at a work center, used for planning and for costing.
Session
Manufacturing➔Job Shop➔Engineering➔Job Shop Routings (tirou4100m000)

Why LN works this way. The routing gives a production order the operations you report as done. Without one, the order has no estimated production costs and nothing to report. A reference operation is a template that brings its own times. Routing Quantity 1 makes those the times for one item.

StepActionYou should see
8.1Check Site at the top is the site from step 1.1Only that site's routings are listed
8.2Product has two filter boxes. Filter the second, for the item, on the made itemNo routing for it yet
8.3Click NewJob Shop Routing (tirou4600m000) opens, with Routing 0, Status = New, today's Effective Date and Routing Quantity 1 filled in
8.4Product has two boxes. Leave the first, for a project, empty, and choose the made item from the lookup on the secondIts description appears
8.5Check Effective Date is not after the BOM's, at step 7.6
8.6Leave Routing, Routing Quantity, Minimum Quantity, Maximum Quantity, Calculate and the lead time fields as LN fills them in
8.7On the Operations grid, click NewLN saves the header, Revision reads 000001, and a new operation line has Operation 10
8.8Press Tab and enter a reference operation you found for the prerequisite in Reference OperationIts description, Work Center and Machine Type fill inWrite downwork center
8.9Scroll the grid right and check the times the reference operation filled in. Don't change them
8.10If Cycle Time (min) is 0, enter how many minutes one made item takesProduction Rate fills in, per hour
8.11Click SaveLead Time fills in
8.12Go back to Job Shop Routings, filter on the made item and tick its row
8.13Click Approve RevisionsLN says the revision was approved, and Status = Approved
8.14Actions➔Use➔Use for Planning
8.15Actions➔Use➔Use for CostingUse for Planning and Use for Costing have green ticks
Build the routing: if something goes wrong
SymptomWhat to do
LN refuses the Work Center or Reference OperationUse one that already exists at your site. Don't make a work center, task or machine here
The operation line won't saveFill in every column the screen marks as needed: at least Operation, Reference Operation and Work Center
The production order has no operationsIts date is before the routing's Effective Date. See step 8.5

9Add the costing rows

Result
Each item has a costing row for your enterprise unit, and LN has worked out its standard cost.
Session
Master Data➔Items➔Items (tcibd0501m000)

Why LN works this way. A standard cost belongs to an enterprise unit, the part of the company that keeps the books for your site. A new item has no row for it, so it has no standard cost at all, and Item - Costing doesn't list it. The made item's cost adds up its materials and its routing, so it goes last.

StepActionYou should see
9.1Filter the list on the first bought item and open itItem (tcibd0501m100) opens
9.2Open the Enterprise Units tabNo rows
9.3On the Enterprise Units grid, click NewItem - Costing (ticpr0107m000) opens for the item, empty
9.4Check Costing Type and Standard Costs BaseLogistics, and ticked
9.5Enter the enterprise unit your warehouses belong to, shown on Warehouses, in Enterprise UnitIts name and financial company appear
9.6Choose Warehouse from its lookupThe lookup offers the item's own warehouse
9.7Choose Scheme from its lookup: the scheme an existing item usesCosting Source fills in: Purchase for a bought item, Job Shop for a made one
9.8Click SaveThe cost components appear, with their costs
9.9Actions➔Calculate and Actualize Standard Costs...Last Actualization Date fills in
9.10Close Item - CostingThe row is on the Enterprise Units grid
9.11Do steps 9.1 to 9.10 for the second bought item
9.12Do steps 9.1 to 9.10 for the made itemCosting Source is Job Shop, and Operation Costs come from the routing
Add the costing rows: if something goes wrong
SymptomWhat to do
The item isn't in Item - CostingIt has no costing row, see step 9.3. Or the list was opened before the row was made: close it and open it again
The made item's cost leaves out its materialsIts materials need their rows first, see step 9.11. A bought item reads 0 until it has a purchase price

10Read the standard costs

Result
You've written down each item's material cost and total cost.
Session
Common➔Standard Costs➔Master Data➔Item - Costing (ticpr0107m000)

Why LN works this way. A production order's cost estimate reads each material's standard cost. A setting decides whether a missing cost stops the estimate or only makes it too low. A bought item gets its standard cost from purchase prices, so a new one usually reads 0.

StepActionYou should see
10.1Open the record for the first bought itemIts costing record, for an enterprise unit
10.2Read Costing SourcePurchase
10.3Open the Standard Cost tab
10.4Read Material Costs and Total CostsWrite downfirst bought item's costs
10.5Do steps 10.1 to 10.4 for the second bought itemWrite downsecond bought item's costs
10.6Do steps 10.1 to 10.4 for the made itemCosting Source is Job ShopWrite downmade item's costs
Read the standard costs: if something goes wrong
SymptomWhat to do
A bought item's cost is 0That's usual for a new item. Its cost comes from purchase prices, which it doesn't have until you buy it
The production order's cost estimate stops with an errorA material may have no standard cost, and a setting makes the estimate stop when one is missing
A cost isn't the one you expectedOpen Item Standard Costs (ticpr3501m000) for the item, on its effective date, to see where the cost came from

Variations

Variations
CaseWhat changes
Two items instead of threeMake one bought item and one made item. It shows both kinds of supply, but the BOM has only one material
A made item with two levelsAdd a part-made item only after the single-level case works. It needs its own item, BOM, routing and costs, and a second production order
A bought finished itemUse another new group whose Default Supply Source is Purchase. It needs no Production defaults, and no BOM or routing
Items only
Task 6		Stop after this task. The items exist but can't be made yet. The next two tasks give the made item its BOM and routing

What comes next

WhenThenStart at
The items, the BOM and the routing are readyBuy the bought items in with Purchase to receiptRead the baseline
The bought items are in stockMake the item with Production order from stockRead the items and their stock
